```{r wf4-bootstrap, include=FALSE}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bootstrap for standalone knitting.
#
# When this document is knitted on its own, the configuration and helper
# functions it depends on are not yet in memory. This chunk loads them by
# extracting the R code out of the corresponding .Rmd files.
#
# When the document is knitted as a child of run_all.Rmd the objects already
# exist, so this chunk does nothing.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
source_rmd <- function(rmd_path) {
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
  knitr::purl(rmd_path, output = tmp, quiet = TRUE)
  source(tmp, local = knitr::knit_global())
  unlink(tmp)
}

if (!exists("sample_name")) {
  source_rmd(here::here("Rmarkdown", "00_setup.Rmd"))
  source_rmd(here::here("Rmarkdown", "01_helpers.Rmd"))
}
```


**PURPOSE**

  WF1, WF2 and WF3 each interrogate the same peak list from a different and
  largely independent angle:

```
    WF1  spectral + retention match to an authentic standard
    WF2  halogen isotope pattern (a physical constant of the nuclide)
    WF3  heteroatom-diagnostic neutral losses and mass defect
```

  None of them is sufficient alone. WF2 is close to decisive within its scope
  but says nothing about compounds that contain no halogen; WF3 is deliberately
  high-recall and therefore low-precision; WF1 depends on the compound being
  present in the in-house library at all.

  WF4 combines them so that a reported identification rests on the CONVERGENCE
  of independent evidence rather than on any single filter. This is what makes
  the assignment defensible: the failure modes of the three workflows are
  different, so agreement between them is meaningful.

INPUT   data_wf4/<sample>_lib_pacs_2ion.csv   (WF1)
```
        data_wf4/<sample>_halo_pacs.csv       (WF2)
        data_wf4/<sample>_hpacs.csv           (WF3)
```
OUTPUT  results_wf4/<sample>_final_PAC_report.csv
```
        results_final/<sample>_final_PAC_report.csv   (delivered copy)
```

```{r wf4-01}
run_wf4 <- function(sample_name) {

  message("\n=== WORKFLOW 4 : evidence integration ===")

  p_lib  <- file.path(dir_data$wf4, paste0(sample_name, "_lib_pacs_2ion.csv"))
  p_halo <- file.path(dir_data$wf4, paste0(sample_name, "_halo_pacs.csv"))
  p_nso  <- file.path(dir_data$wf4, paste0(sample_name, "_hpacs.csv"))

  # Any stream may legitimately be empty (e.g. a sample with no halogenated
  # compounds). Missing inputs are substituted with correctly-typed empty
  # tables so the joins still work and the report is still produced.
  safe_read <- function(path, label) {
    if (file.exists(path)) {
      d <- clean_names(read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE))
      message(sprintf("  %-22s : %d rows", label, nrow(d)))
      d
    } else {
      message(sprintf("  %-22s : MISSING - treated as empty", label))
      NULL
    }
  }

  data_lib  <- safe_read(p_lib,  "WF1 library matches")
  data_halo <- safe_read(p_halo, "WF2 halogenated PACs")
  data_nso  <- safe_read(p_nso,  "WF3 heterocyclic PACs")

  # ---- 4.1 Harmonise coordinates ------------------------------------------
  # The three workflows name their retention-time and mass columns differently.
  # They are renamed to a common vocabulary (t1 / t2 / base_val) so the peaks
  # can be joined.
  data_lib_clean <- if (!is.null(data_lib)) {
    data_lib %>%
      rename(t1 = t1_samp, t2 = t2_samp, base_val = base_mass) %>%
      mutate(t1 = as.numeric(t1), t2 = as.numeric(t2)) %>%
      select(name, t1, t2, acronyms, confidence, matched_ions, area, base_val)
  } else {
    tibble(name = character(), t1 = numeric(), t2 = numeric(),
           acronyms = character(), confidence = character(),
           matched_ions = character(), area = numeric(), base_val = numeric())
  }

  data_halo_clean <- if (!is.null(data_halo)) {
    data_halo %>%
      rename(t1 = rt1_s, t2 = rt2_s, base_val = base_peak) %>%
      mutate(t1 = as.numeric(t1), t2 = as.numeric(t2)) %>%
      select(name, t1, t2, halogen_class, possible_halo_pac, matched_formula,
             detected_isotope_peaks, top2_non_isotope_peaks, base_val)
  } else {
    tibble(name = character(), t1 = numeric(), t2 = numeric(),
           halogen_class = character(), possible_halo_pac = character(),
           matched_formula = character(), detected_isotope_peaks = character(),
           top2_non_isotope_peaks = character(), base_val = character())
  }

  data_nso_clean <- if (!is.null(data_nso)) {
    d <- data_nso %>%
      rename(t1 = x1st_dimension_time_s, t2 = x2nd_dimension_time_s,
             base_val = base_mass) %>%
      mutate(t1 = as.numeric(t1), t2 = as.numeric(t2))
    # max_score is written by WF3 and records the maximum achievable score for
    # whichever scoring scheme was active. Using it (rather than the largest
    # value actually observed) keeps the WF3 bonus on a fixed scale, so results
    # from different samples remain directly comparable.
    if (!"max_score" %in% names(d)) d$max_score <- 8L
    d %>% select(name, t1, t2, base_val, evidence_score, max_score,
                 screening_tier, ref_compound, ref_formula, frag_evidence)
  } else {
    tibble(name = character(), t1 = numeric(), t2 = numeric(), base_val = numeric(),
           evidence_score = numeric(), max_score = numeric(),
           screening_tier = character(),
           ref_compound = character(), ref_formula = character(),
           frag_evidence = character())
  }

  # ---- 4.2 Join on peak identity ------------------------------------------
  # full_join keeps peaks found by ANY workflow, including discoveries seen only
  # by WF2 or WF3 with no library counterpart. coalesce() then fills the unified
  # RT and base-mass columns from whichever stream supplied them.
  combined_data <- data_lib_clean %>%
    full_join(data_halo_clean, by = "name", suffix = c("_lib", "_halo")) %>%
    full_join(data_nso_clean,  by = "name") %>%
    mutate(
      rt1 = coalesce(t1_lib, t1_halo, t1),
      rt2 = coalesce(t2_lib, t2_halo, t2),
      base_mass_peak = coalesce(as.character(base_val_lib),
                                as.character(base_val_halo),
                                as.character(base_val))
    )

  # ---- 4.3 Reliability scoring (0-10) -------------------------------------
  # Library evidence dominates, because a match to an authentic standard on both
  # spectrum and retention time is the strongest evidence available. Halogen and
  # heteroatom evidence act as CORROBORATION, adding up to 2 points each.
  #
  # For peaks with no library hit at all (non-targeted discoveries) the same
  # corroborating evidence is rescaled, so a compound supported by both WF2 and
  # WF3 can still reach a high score without ever appearing in the library.
  final_results <- combined_data %>%
    mutate(
      base_score = case_when(
        str_detect(confidence, "Level 1") ~ 8.0,
        str_detect(confidence, "Level 2") ~ 7.0,
        str_detect(confidence, "Level 3") ~ 7.0,
        TRUE                              ~ 0.0
      ),
      # WF3 contributes proportionally to its evidence score, capped at +2.
      # Normalised by max_score (the scheme maximum) so the bonus does not
      # depend on which peaks happen to be in this particular sample.
      nso_bonus  = ifelse(!is.na(evidence_score) & !is.na(max_score) & max_score > 0,
                          (evidence_score / max_score) * 2, 0.0),
      # WF2 is near-binary: a valid isotope pattern is strong evidence
      halo_bonus = ifelse(!is.na(halogen_class), 2.0, 0.0),

      final_reliability = case_when(
        base_score >  0 ~ pmin(base_score + nso_bonus + halo_bonus, 10.0),
        base_score == 0 ~ (nso_bonus * 2.5) + (halo_bonus * 2.5)
      ),

      # Preferred identity, in order of evidence strength
      primary_identity = case_when(
        !is.na(acronyms)          ~ acronyms,
        !is.na(possible_halo_pac) ~ possible_halo_pac,
        !is.na(ref_compound)      ~ ref_compound,
        TRUE                      ~ name
      ),

      # Which workflows support this peak - makes convergence explicit
      evidence_sources = paste0(
        ifelse(!is.na(acronyms),      "WF1 ", ""),
        ifelse(!is.na(halogen_class), "WF2 ", ""),
        ifelse(!is.na(evidence_score),"WF3", "")
      ) %>% str_trim()
    )

  # ---- 4.4 Deduplicate and export -----------------------------------------
  final_unique <- final_results %>%
    group_by(name) %>%
    slice_max(order_by = final_reliability, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(desc(final_reliability), name) %>%
    select(name, primary_identity, final_reliability, evidence_sources,
           rt1, rt2, base_mass_peak, area,
           confidence, screening_tier, halogen_class,
           matched_ions, detected_isotope_peaks, top2_non_isotope_peaks,
           frag_evidence, matched_formula, ref_formula)

  out_wf4   <- file.path(dir_res$wf4, paste0(sample_name, "_final_PAC_report.csv"))
  out_final <- file.path(dir_final,   paste0(sample_name, "_final_PAC_report.csv"))
  write_csv(final_unique, out_wf4)
  write_csv(final_unique, out_final)

  message(sprintf("  Integrated peaks : %d", nrow(final_unique)))
  print(count(final_unique, evidence_sources, name = "n") %>% arrange(desc(n)))
  message("  Saved: ", basename(out_wf4), "  and  results_final/", basename(out_final))

  invisible(final_unique)
}
```

## Run this stage

The chunk below executes this stage. It runs only when this document is knitted
on its own — when it is knitted as a child of `run_all.Rmd`, that document makes
the call instead, so the stage is not run twice.

```{r wf4-run, eval = !exists(".in_master")}
wf4_out <- run_wf4(sample_name)
```
